coupling_analysis.noise_before_jpeg: Speckle (multiplicative, c=0.28 @sev3) applied before JPEG q18. JPEG quantizes/attenuates the noise: wavelet noise_prior on target-clean residual underestimates (1.1-5.1) and step2 initially reported GAUSSIAN_YCrCb (conf=low, flagged gamma_suspect). Peeling JPEG first is mandatory; §B on peeled residual reveals vm_slope>0.005 → speckle.
coupling_analysis.ycrcb_false_positive: cross_channel_corr 0.68-0.87 is produced by JPEG quantization error of the noisy image: luma-coherent error after RGB->YCbCr->RGB correlates the three channels. rgb_ratio≈1.0 and equal per-channel std prove the noise itself is per-channel RGB (speckle), not YCrCb.
coupling_analysis.extreme_pct_false_positive: peeled extreme_pct 55-62% follows the documented JPEG-residue FP pattern (extreme>50% with noise_prior sigma<5); no impulse noise (impulse would be sparse: zero_ratio of residual 0.08-0.18 means 82-92% of pixels changed).
coupling_analysis.psnr_unreliable: Noise seed mismatch makes pixel PSNR capped ~27 dB for any deterministic simulation; JPEG-only PSNR (25.8-27.8) cannot confirm/deny severity. Selection therefore used signal verification (bb/dct/sigma/FWHM) plus residual statistical fingerprints (std/kurtosis/lag-correlation/intensity scaling), which are seed-independent.
coupling_analysis.order_evidence: JPEG->speckle produces std 37.55 and lag1 0.129 vs target 25.64/0.298 → rejected.
